title: Swap through pointers
description:
Write `void swapViaPointers(int* a, int* b)` that exchanges the two `int`s the pointers point at. You may assume neither pointer is null.

This is the C way of doing what `swapInts(int&, int&)` did in the last lesson. Notice the difference at the call site: the caller has to write `&x` to pass an address.
hints: It is the same three lines as before, but every use of `a` and `b` gains a `*` in front: `*a = *b;` copies the value, while `a = b;` would only re-aim the local pointer.
unitTests:
TEST("swaps the targets") { int x{ 5 }, y{ 9 }; swapViaPointers(&x, &y); CHECK_EQ(x, 9); CHECK_EQ(y, 5); }
TEST("same variable twice is harmless") { int x{ 4 }; swapViaPointers(&x, &x); CHECK_EQ(x, 4); }

grading.unitTests:
TEST("swaps the targets") { int x{ 5 }, y{ 9 }; swapViaPointers(&x, &y); CHECK_EQ(x, 9); CHECK_EQ(y, 5); }
TEST("same variable twice is harmless") { int x{ 4 }; swapViaPointers(&x, &x); CHECK_EQ(x, 4); }
